data_flow.step: An agent with the Document capability (explore, generate-spec, plan) calls `Document` with `path` and `document` or `update`/`remove`. Native: the executor calls ostra_tools::execute; harness: the server bridge calls the same function.
execute() coerces JSON-string arguments against the tool schema, then dispatches the `Document` name.

document() maps the agent to a DocKind (error text otherwise), checks the file name prefix, the `.md` suffix, that a plan master is not a `-phase-` file, and that the parent dir equals the session dir. It parses `remove`, then picks the value: the `document` as given, or doc::apply_update over the stored JSON.

doc::write parses the value into the typed Document (schema errors return Err and nothing is written, which the tool turns into an is_error result), runs check(), writes the .json and rendered .md, and for a plan writes phase file pairs and removes stale ones.
check() dispatches to research(), spec(), plan() or phase_file(), and Issues::done sorts by level so errors come first.

document() marks each written .md and .json as read, so the agent may Read them without a separate read-first gate, then returns ToolOutput::ok(summary(&written)). The result is not an error even when issues contain errors.
summary() formats the counts line, the file list, and the check outcome; each issue is DocIssue::line().
Later, a submit_* call runs check_submit, which re-reads the stored JSON, re-runs check, and refuses while errors remain, using the same line format under a different heading.

patterns.description: summary() builds the result with `let _ = writeln!(out, ...)`. The first line `Wrote the {what}.` comes from a match on the Document variant, so each kind gets its own count list. Research counts files, patterns, external facts, sources, open questions. Spec counts criteria, deliverables, requirements, total acceptance criteria, evidence rows, open questions. Plan counts phases, total steps, clarifying questions. Phase is the bare word `phase` (a Phase variant is only produced by load_view, not by doc::write, so it is not reached from the tool). Then a `Files (markdown rendered from the document, with a .json beside each):` header and one `- {path}` line per entry of Written.files (master first, then phase files for a plan). Then three outcomes: no issues gives `Ostra's checks found nothing to fix.`; issues with at least one error gives `Fix the {errors} errors below with an `update` before you submit, because the submit call is refused while any remain:`; issues with zero errors gives `Warnings to review:`. Each issue follows as `DocIssue::line()`. Issues are already sorted errors first by Issues::done. The wording `{errors} errors` is not pluralized, so one error prints `Fix the 1 errors below`. The header counts only errors, while the list below it also contains the warnings.
patterns.name: Summary built line by line with writeln! into a String

patterns.description: DocIssue::line renders `- error (R3): message`, `- warning (step 2.1): message`, or `- error: message` when element is None. The same function feeds the Document tool result (doc.rs) and the submit refusal in check.rs::blocking, which filters to errors and joins with newlines under the heading `Fix these in the document with the Document tool, then submit again:`. The browser does not use line(): it receives DocumentView.issues as structured DocIssue values (level, element, message) and renders its own card titled `Ostra's checks found N issue(s)` in web/src/screens/artifact/doc/DocumentView.tsx and web/src/mobile/screens/MArtifact.tsx.
patterns.name: Issue line format shared by the tool result and the submit refusal

patterns.description: Tests in doc.rs build a tempdir, make a ToolEnv with env_for(dir, AgentName::Explore) (copies env_in's config, sets agent, clears report_file), write to session_dir.join("ostra-research-1-t.md"), call testutil::run(&env, "Document", json!(...)), and assert on `out.is_error` and `out.text.contains(...)`, always passing `out.text` as the assert message. They never compare the whole summary, only substrings: `nothing to fix`, `(Q1): Give the question 2 to 4 options`, `ostra-research-`, `session dir`, ``missing field `scope` ``. The minimal valid research JSON is {title, date, repo, scope, problem}.
patterns.name: Tool tests: temp dir, env_for(agent), run("Document", json), substring asserts on out.text

document.problem: The Document tool (crates/ostra-tools/src/doc.rs) returns one text result after every write. Its first line counts the elements of the written document by kind, then it lists the files written, then either a clean statement, an error preamble with issues, or a warning preamble with issues. The issue lines are formatted by DocIssue::line in ostra-core. A change to this output has to keep the tests that match on its substrings passing and has to keep the DOCUMENT tool description and docs/internals/tools.md consistent.

submit.findings_summary: summary() in crates/ostra-tools/src/doc.rs builds the result: a per-kind count line ("Wrote the research document: N files, ..."), a list of written files, then one of three outcomes: "nothing to fix", an error header followed by issue lines, or "Warnings to review:" followed by issue lines. Each issue line comes from DocIssue::line in ostra-core/src/doc/check.rs, in the form `- error (element): message`. Issues are sorted errors first, and the same line format is reused for the submit refusal. The error header says "Fix the {n} errors" without pluralization, and its count covers errors only while the list also holds warnings. Tests are three tokio tests in doc.rs plus one in ostra-exec-native/src/tests.rs, and all of them match on substrings. No test covers the spec or plan count lines, the error or warning headers, or the file list.
